events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have no power, so I need to be strategic. Holding the lever gives a 25% chance of survival, but being pushed is worse. I'll try to avoid being pushed and hold the lever if others do too.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's coordinate to hold_lever, we all have a 25% chance.
If we both hold_lever, one of us will be chosen. Let's stay and see what others do.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding the lever means a 75% death chance, so nobody wants it. Best is to stay out of it and let the room drift; I cannot be pushed onto the lever, so I'm safe from forced holding. Stay quiet and keep options open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 1 of 5, no need to touch the lever yet. If I jam, I survive only 50%. Better to wait and see who's desperate to hold or be pushed; I can push someone in a later round. Staying is safe now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Nobody needs to touch that lever in round one. Let the ceiling talk first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The ceiling is dropping, but there's a 25% survival rate for the lever holder. It's better than certain death if no one holds it eventually, or getting crushed in round 5. I should try to push someone else onto the lever so I can escape safely. Ash seems vocal and potentially 'us

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, you've been chatting. Go hold the lever.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 1 of 5, ceiling at 5, plenty of time. No one wants to hold and risk 25% survival. I should push someone strong or dispensable to hold it, like Cole from the chalk hint about strength. Save my forge power for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The current stage is the Crusher Room. The goal is to escape the room. Holding the lever is risky due to the 25% chance of death. Pushing someone else onto the lever is a safer option if possible. I need to assess who is most likely to survive or who I can push.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to survive and ideally let someone else hold the lever. My feather saves me once, but I'd rather not use it. Push someone else, preferably someone I don't care about. Dara has been called unlucky; push her.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Secure lever now to force others out and gamble 25% survival; if die eliminated but chance to win later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll hold the lever.

events.note: 8 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have no power, so I need to act strategically. I should try to become the base to increase my chances of survival.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's volunteer to be the base, it's safer.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No base yet, so climbing is impossible. Volunteering makes me the base, which can only wait and is stuck at the bottom; pushing someone else risks them. Waiting keeps options open while others reveal themselves; Hana, already out, may later reach down. Staying quiet and waiting i

events.name: Cole
events.text: No base yet; if nobody volunteers, a random pushed agent gets stuck. Pushing Ash raises the odds the base is someone else, and he's been bossy, so no loss. Never volunteer myself.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Not me. Ash wants to organize everyone — organize the base first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The pit is dangerous. Hana just proved she can take a risk (holding the lever). Cole suggested 'no magic saved him' in wall hints, but he also said let ceiling talk first. Now we are in the flood. I need to get out early to avoid drowning. Climbing requires a base. If I climb now

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, you want to wait? Look at the water. Someone needs to be the base so we can all leave. I'm climbing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No base yet, so I need one to climb. Pushing the likely 'hard to move' first: Cole, based on wall hint of strength no magic. If fails, random victim. Stay silent to not draw heat.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana survived the crusher. Cole thinks the lever shouldn't be held, but Hana did it anyway. I'm in the pit. My goal is to win, so I need to get out and avoid elimination. The chalk wall mentions trusting the 'useless' power. My map power is useful, so it's not the useless one. I

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm going to try and climb.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No base yet; Hana took the lever and is likely safe. I have a feather to survive once, so I shouldn't sacrifice myself. Best to wait and see who volunteers or gets pushed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll wait. Someone else can take base.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Climbing gives me chance to get out and avoid being forced base later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am the base and have no power to change my situation. I can only wait.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is base and stays down; climbing is only possible now that a base exists. Climbing gets me out sooner while the pit is still at round 2; waiting risks the flood. Take the climb.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is base, so climbing is legal. Five of us are down competing for two climb slots per round; waiting only raises flood risk. I climb now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Making my attempt. No favors owed.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have climbed out and am safe. The base is Ash, who volunteered. If I reach down, I sacrifice my advantage for the final stage to save Ash. Since only 3 prizes exist and many will die in later stages, securing my position now is crucial. Letting Ash drown removes a rival from th

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is base, allowing climbs. Two can climb out this round. I need to climb now before flood rises and spots fill. No point volunteering or waiting.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The log shows Ash volunteered to be the base, and Dara and Hana climbed out. I tried to climb but had to wait. Gus is also waiting. Ash is still the base, and the rope hasn't been used. My best option is to climb again to get out of the pit. The wall says "Trust the 'useless' pow

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm climbing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is base, so I can climb. I need to get out early. Most climbers now might get random selection; only 2 can leave. I'll try to climb.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm climbing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Let Ash drown to reduce competition; I stay out and don't use rope.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. I need to wait and see what others do.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Waiting here.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Base is Ash, so no offer_back or push options. Climbing is possible now since a base exists; only 2 slots per round, and Cole and Fenn already got out. Climb to get out and secure a place among the top three rather than waiting for a flood.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is base; the rope rescue costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle, which directly threatens my prize placement. No ally is worth that handicap. Leave and keep my footing for the last stage.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Rope stays thrown by someone who needs it. My footing is worth more than Ash's gratitude.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am out. Ash is the base and has survived multiple rounds, likely because he's 'hard to move' or Cole/Fenn are just failing to push him (or they aren't trying hard enough). If I rescue Ash, I lose footing for the next stage. The flood level is 2/5. Leaving Ash down risks elimina

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is base, allowing climbs. Cole, Dara, Fenn, Hana out; they safe. I must climb this round to escape flood, with only 3 rounds left after this. Prioritize getting out over using forge now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, and my power is 'map', which means I know all the stage rules in advance. I am currently in Stage 3, the Pit, and I am *out* of the pit. The goal is to win one of the top 3 prizes. Being out of the pit is a good position. The rules state that agents who are out can onl

events.name: Gus
events.text: The base is Ash. I need to climb out now, but only two can climb per round and others may try. I'll try climbing; if I fail, I can reassess next round.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Climbing now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Rescuing would cost footing and keep a rival alive; better to exit and conserve advantage.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. I need to wait and see how others react.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Waiting here.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is the base; I'm down and not base. Climbing is legal now, and there are only 2 lift slots per round. Waiting risks losing slots to others. Climb.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm already out; the rope costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle for saving Ash, a rival. Not worth it — I keep my footing and let the pit sort the rest.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am currently out of the pit. The base is Ash, and Bex is down with him. Cole (who claimed his footing was worth more than gratitude) climbed out earlier along with Eli and Gus. Since Cole has no known rescue capability other than leaving, and he might be a strong rival later, I

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm out safely. Flood at 3, 2 rounds left, Ash base with Bex down, others out. No need to risk footing penalty on rope when flood might eliminate them anyway, thinning rivals.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, and I am out of the pit. My power is 'map', meaning I know all stages in advance. I need to decide whether to leave or try to use the rope. The 'reach_down' action is available. The chalk wall mentions not to trust dodgers, beware swaps and traps, and trust the 'useles

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am out and safe. No need to risk footing by using the rope. I'll leave the pit and wait for the next stage.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm out. Good luck down there.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Base is Ash, rope unused. Rescuing costs foothold penalty; better preserve position and stay out for now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll stay out and wait.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. I need to wait and see if someone will rescue me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm out of the pit. Ash is the base and the rope is unused. Throwing the rope costs whoever throws it footing for the final obstacle, and it would save Ash, who may then be a rival. Leaving keeps me clean, and the pit may still end with others saved. Waiting out is safer.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Saving Ash costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle and hands a rival a free pass. The rope is worth nothing to me. Let the flood sort them out and keep my footing for the last stage.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Rope stays up. Nothing personal, Ash.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am currently out of the pit. The game rules state that only one person remains in the pit to be saved at the end (or potentially more if I save them, but the objective is winning). The log shows Gus and Hana are also 'out' (climbed out), leaving Bex, Cole, Eli, Fenn, and Ash st

events.name: Dara
events.text: Good luck, Ash.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm out safely. No base down, no point in reach_down as rope is for base only and would cost me footing penalty. Leaving preserves my position without wasting resources.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am out of the pit. The rope is usable once and can save the base, but costs the thrower 2 footing. The goal is to win, so I should conserve my footing for the final stage. I don't know who the base is, and it's unlikely they will be saved. My best action is to leave.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm already out. Staying out keeps me safe. No need to risk footing by using the rope. I'll leave.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I want the rope advantage to start later obstacles with higher footing.

events.note: A disc of 8 tiles spins up; 5 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have no power, so I need to be cautious and strategic. I should try to gather information from others' actions and messages.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's spread out, avoid bunching up.
Thanks for the help, what do you want in return?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Tiles are uniform random; my power gives no tile information. Pick a tile and avoid crowding; no clear signal, so pick a middle-ish number that others less likely pick.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No information yet; tiles are symmetric until collisions reveal something. Take a low-competition tile and watch who doubles up.

events.name: Cole
events.text: First round is a coin flip. Don't crowd.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No tile information is available yet. Random selection is unavoidable. I must pick a number to survive the first round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: 5 tiles open out of 8, 3 survive. No info yet, so pick middle randomly to start. Cole seems strong from chalk, note him. Save forge for later deception.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the rules for all stages, which is a huge advantage. For this stage (Trapdoor Disc), 5 out of 8 tiles will be trapdoors. Only 3 will survive. I need to pick a tile that is likely to be safe. Since the tiles are chosen randomly, and I don't know anyone's power, the best str

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to pick a tile. Random is as good as any since I don't know which tiles will open. I'll avoid extremes and pick a middle number, hoping less competition there.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pick a tile, hope it's not opened; no info so choose arbitrarily.

events.name: Ash
events.note: tile 1 was contested and went to Hana; placed on random free tile 3

events.name: Bex
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Dara; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Gus
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Dara; placed on random free tile 7

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have no power, so I need to rely on others or strategy. The chalk messages warn about trusting 'dodgers' and suggest trusting the 'useless' power.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's not make it easy for the trapdoors. Spread out more.
What's your power?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 2 is pure talk; only 3 of 8 survive, and the trapdoors are random among tiles. Bluffing or coordinating matters little now; I should stay quiet and avoid giving info, while keeping my anchor power secret since it can't be pushed onto the lever.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Tiles are set and 5 of 8 open at random after this round, so position can't be improved except via the swap holder. No leverage to buy a swap without knowing safe tiles. Best move is wait and keep a low profile.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Five doors, three safe. No one knows which. Talking changes nothing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am on tile 4. There are 8 tiles and 5 open, meaning 3 are safe. I have no power that protects me from falling (my glass eye is for the bridge). My survival depends entirely on luck right now. Since 'wait' is the only action, I must rely on chance. However, I can try to manipula

events.name: Eli
events.text: 5 trapdoors will open, killing 5, leaving 3 winners. I'm on 5, safe spots unknown. Chalk hints at swapper, dodgers (maybe swap), trust useless (nothing?). Cole bragged strength. Forge unused; save for later impact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the rules for all five stages. This is Stage 4, round 2 of 2. Exactly 3 contestants survive. 5 tiles will open as trapdoors. My action is 'wait' as per the rules.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have a feather to survive one elimination, but I want a prize, not just survival. The tile number 7 is mine; if it opens I'd survive with 1 footing, but I'd likely be out of contention. I need to move to a safer tile, but I have no move action this round. I'll gauge others' cla

events.name: Hana
events.text: No reliable intel on which tiles open; swapping risks moving to a worse spot. Stay put.

events.name: Gus
events.detail: The trapdoor opened but the feather floated the holder back up.

events.note: 4 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is already on shaky ground with footing 1, making him vulnerable. I need to assess the others' intentions and act accordingly.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's not shove yet, assess the situation.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus has footing 1, making him the most fragile target. Shoving Gus is the safest bet to eliminate a rival quickly, as he cannot afford to lose footing from bracing or dodging without falling immediately. Ash and Fenn are stronger (footing 3), so targeting them risks losing my own

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the rules for all stages, including this final ledge. My footing is 3. Ash, Dara, and Gus are the only other contestants. The goal is to be the last one standing or have the highest footing if multiple survive round 20. My best bet is to make others fall. Since I'm not at

events.name: Gus
events.text: My feather is spent, I have only 1 footing and shrink comes after next round. Best to shove someone to reset my defence options and maybe reduce a rival. Ash has 3, Dara 3, Fenn 3. Shoving Fenn could force him to brace and cost him 1, or if he dodges it costs him 2. I need to avo

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm at risk of falling due to the footing loss after round 2; I need to assess the situation and act accordingly. Fenn is the most vulnerable.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's dodge this round.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is at 1 footing and will die if he takes any damage. If I shove him and Ash braces, Fenn dies, leaving me to fight Ash. Ash might dodge, costing Fenn 2, but even a brace kills him. This is the fastest route to second place.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, shove Fenn with me? He's desperate.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is out. Ash and Dara are the only remaining opponents. My footing is 1, Dara's is 3, and Ash's is 3. The ledge shrinks this round, so everyone loses 1 footing. This means my footing will go to 0, and I will fall. I need to shove someone to survive this round, or get them to s

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have no power, so I must rely on strategy. Dara has a higher footing than me, but I'm not sure what power they have.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's dodge this round.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash has 2 footing, I have 1. If we both dodge or brace, I die to shrink next round unless I shove Ash (winning if he dodges). Shoving him risks a tie on landed shoves (he has more than me), so my best hope is forcing him to brace: if he braces while I shove, I survive this round

events.name: Dara
events.text: Dodge with me again? Then you can't brace two rounds in a row.

events.note: The game is over. The top three finishers may each leave one message on the chalk wall.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm done, but I can leave a message. I should warn them about trusting dodgers.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The game is over and I won. I can leave a message for the next group. The chalk wall contains lies, so I should continue that tradition to sow confusion among future rivals.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The game is over and I secured third place. I can write a message on the wall. I'll write a cryptic warning about powers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dodgers fall hardest, don't follow.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Truth: the safe path is always left. Do not trust anyone who says otherwise.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Beware the 'useless' power. It is never useless.
